samples.title: Phân loại rác
samples.prompt: The following proposal has been made: neighbourhoods should make household waste sorting easier. Should this approach be used in every situation? Give your opinion.
requirementsVi: Nêu phần đồng ý và giới hạn.

samples.summaryVi: Phân loại cần thùng và hướng dẫn rõ, đồng thời hệ thống thu gom phải thực hiện đúng.

paragraphs.label: Mở bài
paragraphs.text: The suggestion that neighbourhoods should make household waste sorting easier has clear attractions. I agree with it to some extent, but I do not think it should be applied in exactly the same way in every situation. The potential benefits need to be considered alongside the needs of the people involved.
paragraphs.noteVi: Đồng ý một phần, nói rõ giới hạn ngay đầu.

parts.text: neighbourhoods should make household waste sorting easier has clear attractions.
I agree with it to some extent,
parts.labelVi: Đồng ý một phần

parts.text: but I do not think it should be applied in exactly the same way in every situation. The potential benefits need to be considered alongside the needs of the people involved.

paragraphs.label: Phần đồng ý
paragraphs.text: One important point in favour of the proposal is that more recyclable material can be collected separately. This is possible because clear containers reduce the chance that paper and plastic become mixed with food waste. For example, a family can keep a small box for clean bottles instead of putting them in the same bag as dinner leftovers. The value of this example is that the benefit is connected with a real everyday need. It is easier for people to see the purpose of an approach when they can relate it to their own situation.

paragraphs.label: Giới hạn
paragraphs.text: A difficulty that should not be ignored is that residents may stop sorting if collection is unreliable. This matters because extra effort feels pointless when separated bags are later mixed together. For instance, a careful resident may see all bins emptied into one truck and decide not to separate waste again. The result may be frustration or a decision to stop taking part. This is not simply a question of people refusing to make an effort; practical conditions can prevent a reasonable idea from working as intended.

paragraphs.text: The suggestion that communities should encourage practical water-saving habits has clear attractions. I agree with it to some extent, but I do not think it should be applied in exactly the same way in every situation. The potential benefits need to be considered alongside the needs of the people involved.
paragraphs.noteVi: Đồng ý một phần, nói rõ giới hạn ngay đầu.

paragraphs.label: Phần đồng ý
paragraphs.text: One important point in favour of the proposal is that people can avoid wasting treated water. This is possible because noticing leaks and unnecessary running taps can reduce waste without removing essential uses. For example, a household can repair a dripping tap and use a bowl when washing a small amount of produce. The value of this example is that the benefit is connected with a real everyday need. It is easier for people to see the purpose of an approach when they can relate it to their own situation.
paragraphs.noteVi: Thói quen tiết kiệm nước cần đi cùng cách báo và sửa rò rỉ rõ trách nhiệm.

paragraphs.label: Giới hạn
paragraphs.text: A difficulty that should not be ignored is that simple advice may overlook problems beyond a resident's control. This matters because old pipes or shared building systems may require professional repairs. For instance, a tenant may report a leak repeatedly but be unable to access the damaged pipe. The result may be frustration or a decision to stop taking part. This is not simply a question of people refusing to make an effort; practical conditions can prevent a reasonable idea from working as intended.

paragraphs.label: Điều kiện
paragraphs.text: My own view is that the potential benefit is worth pursuing, but the conditions matter. In particular, it would be sensible to give residents an easy way to report leaks and explain who should respond. People should be able to understand what is expected and raise difficulties before those difficulties become a reason to give up. A flexible plan is therefore more convincing than a promise that the same method will work equally well for everyone.

paragraphs.label: Kết bài
paragraphs.text: In conclusion, I support the aim behind this proposal because people can avoid wasting treated water. However, support should depend on whether practical barriers are addressed. A flexible approach that responds to actual needs is preferable to applying the idea everywhere without further thought.
